clue.text: System that's used for tax

parts.note: pro is Latin for 'for', as in pros and cons
a cess is an old word for a tax or levy

explanation.surface: A tax regime is described as the system used for collecting tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's used' is linking padding; 'for' supplies its Latin equivalent before the tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A procedure or method of doing things is a system; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Complain bitterly about extremely dear carriage from US

parts.note: to rail is to complain bitterly
ca, for circa, means about
the extreme, final letter of the word dear

explanation.surface: A traveller complains bitterly about a very expensive carriage imported from the US.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is CA (circa), not a containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage this is a railway passenger coach, a kind of carriage.

clue.text: An infirm Republican? It's what some believe

indicators.note: the clue's 'infirm' is split as 'in firm', and 'in' places the Republican inside the firm

parts.note: a firm is a company, abbreviated CO
red is the colour of the Republican party on US electoral maps

explanation.surface: A sickly Republican politician is the subject of a statement of belief.
explanation.walkthrough: The container lives inside one word: 'infirm' must be split as 'in firm', supplying both the containment and the company abbreviation. 'An' is padding.
explanation.definitionFit: A creed is a statement of the principles a group of people hold true.

clue.text: Fish given second light touch to dorsal area

parts.note: a tickle is a light touch
dorsal refers to the back

explanation.surface: A fish gets a quick tickle on its back.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small spiny freshwater fish, so an example of fish.

clue.text: Experienced surgeon operated on European

indicators.note: in an across clue 'operated on European' puts the operated word after the European one

parts.note: a vet is an animal surgeon
ran, as a machine runs or operates

explanation.surface: A seasoned surgeon has operated on a patient from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'operated on' looks like surgery, but 'on' just places RAN after E.
explanation.definitionFit: Used adjectivally, the word describes someone with long service and much practice, hence experienced.

clue.text: Going out with topless degenerate

indicators.note: topless removes the top, first letter, in a down clue

parts.note: to regress is to degenerate or go backwards

explanation.surface: Someone goes out on the town in a topless outfit, looking degenerate.
explanation.definitionFit: Egress is the act of leaving or exiting a place, a formal word for an exit.

clue.text: Hedonistic EU prince travelling round Austria

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the letter for Austria
travelling suggests the letters moving about into a new order

parts.note: A is the international vehicle code for Austria

explanation.surface: A pleasure-seeking European royal tours Austria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges EU PRINCE; 'round' puts that around A.
explanation.definitionFit: Devoted to sensual pleasure and fine living, after Epicurus, so a synonym for hedonistic.

clue.text: Solution has T in place of second P in European port

indicators.note: T takes the place of the letter for second within the word for solution

parts.note: an answer is a solution

explanation.surface: An instruction to swap letters in the name of a European port, like a puzzle note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second P' looks like the second letter P; in fact 'second' is S, and P is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Antwerp is a major Belgian seaport on the Scheldt, an example of a European port.

clue.text: See 16
Police dog that's bound to see evening shower?

indicators.note: the dog is bound to (attached after) the seeing word, so that word comes first

parts.note: Five-O is US slang for the police, from the TV series Hawaii Five-O
to clock something is slang for to notice or see it
to shadow someone is to dog or follow them

explanation.surface: A police dog is trained to spot something worth seeing in the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evening shower' is not rain: it is something that shows in the evening, stubble grown since the morning shave.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubble that appears late in the day is jokingly something that shows up in the evening.

clue.text: Bars supply north-east district

indicators.note: read as 'supplely', in a supple, bendy way, so the letters are flexed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sources goods for a district in the north-east of a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a verb but is the adverb from supple, signalling the anagram of NE plus DISTRICT.
explanation.definitionFit: To interdict is to forbid or prohibit, so it is a verb meaning bars.

clue.text: See 10
Cleavages Simon Peter and Andrew perhaps found pronounced

indicators.note: pronounced signals that the word is said aloud, giving a near sound-alike

parts.note: the apostles Simon Peter and his brother Andrew were fishermen, so examples of fishers

explanation.surface: The apostles Peter and Andrew discover splits or divisions among people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' is a link word; the fishermen apostles give FISHERS, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cracks or splits in rock are cleavages in the geological sense, narrow openings.

clue.text: Politician leading English party? False!

indicators.note: the politician leads, so comes in front of the rest

parts.note: Donald Trump is a politician
the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A politician heads up an English party, and someone shouts that it is false.
explanation.definitionFit: Charges that are fabricated or concocted are false ones; the adjective is used of accusations.

clue.text: Saint Mungo relocated, with Glasgow initially out of range?

indicators.note: relocated means the letters are moved to new places
out says that letter is left out of the rearranged fodder
initially takes the first letter of Glasgow

explanation.surface: Glasgow's patron saint, Mungo, has moved out of the city's range.
explanation.walkthrough: Saint Mungo is the patron saint of Glasgow; 'relocated' rearranges SAINT MUNGO minus G ('Glasgow initially', 'out').
explanation.definitionFit: A range of hills is a chain of mountains, so the plural noun matches.

clue.text: Maintain one's composure as warder, say, after row during meal left one a little peeved

indicators.note: the spoken part is followed by what comes after it in the clue
say signals the word as spoken; in a non-rhotic accent it matches the first two words of the answer

parts.note: a prison warder is a keeper

indicators.note: the row happens during the meal, so it sits inside it

parts.note: supper is an evening meal
a tiff is a minor row or quarrel
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: a little of the word peeved is just its first letter

explanation.surface: A prison officer is told to stay calm after a dinner-time quarrel left someone slightly annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: KEEPER only sounds like KEEP A to non-rhotic (mostly British) ears, where the final R is silent; 'say' signals that. 'after' is loose: the warder's part actually comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means staying calm and unemotional in adversity, keeping one's composure.

clue.text: Bill gets sheep to behave badly

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill
a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: A man named Bill gets his sheep to misbehave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a name; it is an account, AC.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to misbehave or show off, particularly of children or machines.

clue.text: Start to climb tree above a volcanic crater

indicators.note: the start of the word climb is its first letter

parts.note: the alder is a tree

explanation.surface: A climber starts up a tree above a volcano's crater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'above' places the pieces in order in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A caldera is a large basin formed when a volcano collapses, a kind of volcanic crater.

clue.text: Essential oil obtained from fish in tin? Difficult, if unopened

indicators.note: in here means placed within, as a fish packed in a tin sits inside the can

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
a pike is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: with its opening letter removed

parts.note: hard means difficult

explanation.surface: Getting oil from a tinned fish is tricky if the can stays shut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tin' is the chemical symbol, not a can, and 'unopened' means losing the first letter, not staying sealed.
explanation.definitionFit: Spikenard is an aromatic oil from a Himalayan plant, an example of an essential oil.

clue.text: Disputed region ready for broadcast on space station

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits on top of the second
broadcast means spoken on air, so it is the sound that counts

parts.note: ready money, or the readies, is cash
Mir was the Soviet/Russian space station

explanation.surface: Something about a disputed territory is ready to be broadcast from a space station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' is money, CASH, sounded as KASH.
explanation.definitionFit: Kashmir is a territory contested between India and Pakistan, a disputed region.

clue.text: Bit of catarrh on child producing wheezing sounds

indicators.note: only a bit of the run of words catarrh on child is used, the letters sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A child with catarrh is making wheezy breathing noises.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhonchi are rattling or snoring chest sounds heard through a stethoscope, typically in obstructed airways.

clue.text: This setter's having quiet drink to follow Vlad's example

parts.note: the setter says 'I'm', this setter is
P (piano) means quiet in music
ale is a drink

explanation.surface: The setter, sipping a quiet drink, plans to copy Vlad.
explanation.walkthrough: Vlad the Impaler, the Wallachian prince, skewered his enemies on stakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Vlad III was notorious for skewering victims on stakes, so copying him means doing that.

clue.text: 5 12, perhaps

definitions.meaning: the answer to 5 across is a veteran, someone long experienced
the answer to 12 across can be read as O (old) plus a clock, which is a timer

explanation.walkthrough: 12 across is O'CLOCK; read O as the abbreviation for old and a clock as a timer.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-serving person is a veteran; an antique clock is an aged timekeeper, a second sense.

clue.text: See 10
Superior article at front of book on autonomous computer program

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: the front of the word book is its first letter

parts.note: a bot is a program that acts automatically

explanation.surface: A superior article is at the front of a book about software bots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Superior' is a noun: the head of a religious house.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of an abbey is its superior, as Father Superior names the senior monk.

clue.text: Bad idea, beginning to interview Trump in warm bathroom

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters are spoiled and need reforming
the beginning of the word interview, its first letter

explanation.surface: It is a bad idea to start interviewing Donald Trump in a heated bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' rearranges IDEA, I (from 'beginning to interview') and TRUMP together.
explanation.definitionFit: In a Roman bath complex this was the room of moderate heat, between the hot and cold rooms.

clue.text: See 4
Old man? Man possibly unknown in Scottish town

parts.note: one's old man is one's father, pa
the Isle of Man is an example of an isle
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: An old man, possibly an unknown one, lives in a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person; capitalised, it is the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Paisley is a large town west of Glasgow in Renfrewshire, Scotland.

clue.text: Send letter to us that's left out? On the contrary, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it signals that the phrase is said aloud

parts.note: the opposite of left out taken word by word is right in

explanation.surface: A newspaper invites anyone who feels excluded to write to it.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap each word of 'left out' for its opposite to get RIGHT IN, which is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To write in is to send a letter to an organisation such as a newspaper or broadcaster.
